entries.title: Senior Software Engineer & IT Consultant
bullets: Technical lead and main point of contact for a long-running project at an international logistics provider, covering carrier applications and integration with the client's transport management landscape.
Own the architecture decisions within my project scope, from integration concepts through data processing logic to error handling.

Designed and built a status application that consolidates shipment data from heterogeneous carrier sources and manually entered TMS records into reliable status information from a freight forwarder's perspective — including data cleanup and matching logic for cases where carriers provide no unambiguous identifier (air and ocean).
Designed the ingestion path around Kafka as a buffering and throttling layer for high-volume inbound data.
Integrated a legacy transport management system via EDI, including development on the PL/SQL side.
Replaced fragmented document handling with a central document service backed by S3 — over 80,000 documents processed in the first two weeks.
Delivered applications spanning bookings, sailing schedules and status processing, working closely with product management, QA and business stakeholders.
Maintain and extend shared libraries used across projects, including integration of a new permission model.

entries.title: Software Engineer & IT Consultant
bullets: Tech Lead (late 2023 – April 2024): technical lead for a team of six developers, responsible for architecture decisions and code quality.
Designed the database schema and internal data structures underlying the carrier applications.

Built the ingestion process for provider data — retrieving files from SFTP endpoints, transforming them into the internal data model, and notifying the target system across five globally distributed instances.
Delivered custom software for an international logistics provider from concept through to deployment, connecting modern services to established legacy platforms.

entries.title: Founder & Application Developer
bullets: Founder of Bostrot, developing and commercially distributing developer tools with a combined {{TOTAL_STARS}}+ GitHub stars and an active user community.

WSL Manager — a Flutter/Dart GUI for managing WSL2 environments with {{WSL_DOWNLOADS}}+ downloads, shipped through the Microsoft Store, Winget, Scoop and Chocolatey, localized into 9 languages, with a built-in MCP server for AI agents such as Claude Desktop.
Telegram & Signal Support Bot — a TypeScript ticketing system with Docker deployment, also operated as a hosted commercial service.
PowerToys Run Winget Plugin — a C# plugin for Microsoft PowerToys enabling package search and installation.
Published reusable open-source packages on pub.dev, including a Plausible Analytics client and a chunked downloader for Dart/Flutter.
Own the full product lifecycle across all projects: architecture, implementation, release management, distribution, community support and monetization.

entries.title: Student Software Engineer & IT Tutor
bullets: Engineered and maintained backend infrastructure for production teaching systems used across lab courses, improving the architecture and code quality of a Jenkins-based CI submission system and the MoniTutor feedback platform.

Built a cross-platform CI/CD pipeline (Windows, Linux, macOS on x86 and ARM) delivering a portable, preconfigured VS Code C++ toolchain, plus a custom VS Code extension that simplified lab assignment workflows for first-year students.

Bachelor thesis (grade 1.0): architecture modernization of MoniTutor — migrated the core client from Python to Rust, substantially improving runtime performance, memory footprint and stability. Deployed to production lab courses immediately after completion.
Mentored first-year students in C++ and core computer science concepts as a programming tutor.

entries.title: Teaching Assistant — C++
bullets: Mentored first-semester computer science students in foundational programming concepts and C++.
Ran the departmental Q&A tutorial, answering technical questions from computer science students as well as students from other engineering programs.
Reviewed student code and guided hands-on debugging sessions.
